title: Competitive exclusion in a chemostat with unequal removal rates
decision_reason: Full primary formulation and independent scholarly corroboration, later model/theorem comparisons, duplicate checks and separated A46 adversarial self-review passed; no unresolved material matching resolution claim.
aliases: competitive exclusion for general monotone chemostat growth

problem_fingerprint.objects: Any positive integer n, D>0, S_in>0 and d_i>0; C^1 growth functions f_i:[0,infinity)->[0,infinity), f_i(0)=0, f_i'(s)>0 for s>0. Each f_i(lambda_i)=d_i has a finite positive solution.
problem_fingerprint.model: S'=D(S_in-S)-sum_i f_i(S)x_i; x_i'=(f_i(S)-d_i)x_i. Constant yield coefficients normalized to one by biomass rescaling.
problem_fingerprint.quantifiers: For every such model with 0<lambda_1<lambda_2<=...<=lambda_n and lambda_1<S_in, and every initial state S(0)>=0, x_i(0)>0, ask whether every solution converges to the single-winner equilibrium.
problem_fingerprint.observable: lim S(t)=lambda_1; lim x_1(t)=D(S_in-lambda_1)/d_1; lim x_i(t)=0 for i>=2 as t->infinity.
problem_fingerprint.conclusion: Prove or disprove global convergence to the lowest-break-even species. Species removal constants may differ freely from one another and from nutrient dilution D.
problem_fingerprint.scope: Single well-mixed resource, autonomous ODE, constant yields, strictly increasing growth functions and a strict unique best competitor. No variable yields, density-dependent growth, immigration, seasonal forcing, inhibition, stochasticity, spatial diffusion or restricted Monod response. One family across n and kinetic parameters.

resolution_comparisons.result: Constant-yield Monod/Holling-II kinetics admit a Lyapunov proof with different species removals. Common washout and monotone response results are also reviewed.
resolution_comparisons.difference: Arbitrary C1 strictly increasing response functions need not be Monod functions, and d_i are not required to equal D.

resolution_comparisons.result: Theorem 2 allows variable yields with a crossing condition and constants alpha_i separating response ratios. Theorem 3 restates the constant-yield Wolkowicz–Lu sufficient condition (8).
resolution_comparisons.difference: The additional max/min ratio-separation condition is not a hypothesis of the candidate. The introduction explicitly says suitable constants cannot be found for every growth function. Constant-yield specialization is checked, not inferred from the paper title.

resolution_comparisons.result: Global convergence follows from winner-crossing and nutrient-balance conditions plus an interspecies inequality with a positive constant for each invadable competitor.
resolution_comparisons.difference: In Theorem 4.1, f_1(S)p_i(S)>c_i f_i(S)p_1(S) for 0<S<1 is an extra condition. Here that source’s f_i denotes net growth, p_i uptake; the candidate’s f_i is gross growth. No assumption that these inequalities follow from monotonicity is made.

resolution_comparisons.result: Positive nonstationary periodic solutions are excluded when f_i(s)<1+f_j(s)+(1-s)p_j_prime(s)/p_j(s), in the normalized net-growth/uptake notation, for all i!=j and 0<s<1.
resolution_comparisons.difference: The extra inequality is not automatic for arbitrary responses/removals. Excluding periodic solutions is weaker than establishing every trajectory’s convergence in arbitrary dimension.

resolution_comparisons.result: General increasing growth functions yield exclusion when one common D appears in every removal term.
resolution_comparisons.difference: The model requires d_i=D, while the candidate allows arbitrary positive d_i. The abstract’s broad phrase about increasing growth does not remove this model restriction.

resolution_comparisons.result: Each compact initial-state set keeping the winning species above a positive threshold admits a sufficiently small exchange perturbation with convergence to a perturbed equilibrium.
resolution_comparisons.difference: The unperturbed system has common removal u. The exchange vector must sum to zero for every state and vanish at perturbation zero. Terms (u-d_i)x_i do not satisfy that identity for arbitrary d_i. No iteration of local perturbation stability is justified to all removal parameters. Journal model preview agrees; full journal theorem not directly read.

resolution_comparisons.result: Convergence when maximal-fitness strains carry positive initial mass; an explicit measure-valued counterexample without that mass oscillates around a circle of fitness maxima.
resolution_comparisons.difference: Finite support specializes to f_i(S)=alpha_i gamma_i S, a linear response family. The counterexample uses the pushforward of e^(-tau) d tau along an infinite spiral with zero initial mass on the limiting circle. Finite n, strict unique lowest break-even and positive x_1(0) exclude this mechanism.

resolution_comparisons.result: A conditional convergence criterion for three-dimensional competitive flows; clock-model applications impose additional compound-matrix conditions.
resolution_comparisons.difference: The candidate has arbitrary dimension n+1 and opposite-sign substrate/species cross derivatives, not the displayed all-off-diagonal-nonpositive model. Absence or orbital stability of periodic orbits is an additional assumption, not proved for the candidate.

resolution_comparisons.result: Chaotic food-chain dynamics are investigated with predation between trophic levels.
resolution_comparisons.difference: Y consumes X and Z consumes Y; their growth depends on other species concentrations. This is not the candidate model, where every population grows only through the common nutrient. Classified from the full displayed model and discussion, not the abstract; numerical proof itself not audited.

resolution_comparisons.result_scope: Global convergence subject to extra response-ratio separation constants.
resolution_comparisons.mismatch: The additional max/min inequalities are not assumed in the candidate. This is the same conditional class already distinguished through Sari–Mazenc.

mathematical_checks: Constants yields are positive constants and can be absorbed by x_i=original_biomass_i/Y_i. No variable yield is silently admitted.
Setting all derivatives to zero at the winner yields x_1=D(S_in-lambda_1)/d_1. The D factor is kept; one preceding line in H05’s proof appears to omit it, while model (2.9)’s equilibrium includes it.

For M=S+sum_i x_i, M_prime=D*S_in-D*S-sum_i d_i*x_i <= D*S_in-min(D,d_1,...,d_n)*M. Together with local C1 uniqueness and positivity this excludes finite-time blow-up; convergence is the actual open demand.

The strict gap applies only between lambda_1 and the remaining break-even values. Ties among losing species are allowed. n=1 is explicitly vacuous in the ordering tail and already solved; it does not receive a separate count.
All populations are initially positive, avoiding absence of the proposed winner. S(0)=0 is allowed; positive feed drives S into the positive region.
All finite n and arbitrary allowed kinetic parameters form one canonical question. No arbitrary-data, species-number or common-D variants are separately counted.

Shi–Bai–Bao, Dynamics of an unstirred chemostat model with intra- and interspecific competition, DOI 10.3934/dcdsb.2026053, was a discovery lead. The full-theorem page requires access; public PDF links returned empty/404. No full theorem reading or proof certification is claimed. It is not used as a formulation or status source, or as evidence that the finite well-mixed conjecture is resolved.
The 2017 recycle-sludge paper DOI 10.1007/s10441-017-9309-4 was seen through PubMed metadata/abstract only and is supplementary discovery, not independent full-text corroboration.

The 2025 plasmid/toxin paper DOI 10.1142/S0218339025500354 appeared as a discovery hit; primary full text was not retrieved and no theorem-level assessment is claimed. No admission evidence is taken from its abstract.
The McMaster file 28731.pdf is a delayed chemostat paper, not the Wolkowicz–Lu constant-yield source. The latter is assessed through SM11 Theorem 3’s full restatement, not a misidentified PDF.
Berlin-hosted FH09 PDF failed TLS hostname validation; the public NTHU author copy was read instead. No certificate validation was bypassed.
